target_customer: Orthopedic and hand surgeons and the hospitals or surgery centers that buy surgical biologics for tendon, ligament and muscle repair
problem: Internal scarring and adhesions after tendon or ligament surgery restrict motion and worsen recovery. Existing barriers are hard to shape and wrap around tendons.
business_model: Medical device sold to surgical sites per procedure (flowable ECM based gel, B3 GEL System)
product_category: Surgical biologic, anti-adhesion tissue protection gel

founders.name: Tim Keane
education: PhD in bioengineering, University of Pittsburgh
founders.background_notes: YC page cites regenerative medicine and biomaterials expertise, over 30 publications, and a Biodesign Fellowship at Texas Medical Center before TYBR.

founders.name: Alex Smith
education: BS and MEng in Biomedical Engineering, Texas A&M University
PhD in Mechanical Engineering, University of Houston
founders.background_notes: YC page cites nearly a decade of medical device development (dialysis access, vaginal dilators, ventricular assist pump design). Employers are not named.

competitors.name: Seprafilm (film adhesion barrier)
competitors.what: Established bioresorbable film barrier used to limit post surgical adhesions; a review describes it as expensive, fragile, quickly degrading and difficult to shape or wrap around tendons
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent product on the market; no figures seen
competitors.funding_then: Not applicable (product of an established company, owner not verified here)

technical_complexity.rationale: A naturally derived ECM hydrogel with a spray delivery system had to be formulated, tested in animals and taken through FDA 510(k) review, which came in June 2025 per press releases. Hard for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Clearance, biomaterial know how and clinical evidence take years to replicate, but at founding there was no clearance and no patent evidence seen in sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source seen showing an incumbent copying or buying TYBR through 2026; it raised a $30M Series A in July 2026 and stayed independent.

market_need_then: A 2021 review of anti-adhesion materials notes most tendon adhesion materials were still at animal testing stage and existing barriers have cost, degradation and handling limits. YC cites millions of Americans having tendon or ligament surgery each year.

branding.domain_note: tybrhealth.com, a prefix style domain with Health added to the invented name (date not found)

identity.logo: Standalone B3 Gel product logo alongside the TYBR wordmark
identity.visual_style: Clinical and modern, blue gel vial imagery with orange curved graphics
identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical and benefit focused, surgeon testimonial led

branding.brand_signature: The brilliant blue color of the B3 GEL, described as aiding precise application

brand_strength.rationale: Product brand B3 GEL is used on the site, but no press about the brand itself, no community and no merch were found. Name origin is not public.

outcome_analysis: TYBR stayed active and independent. It moved from an NIH funded ECM spray concept to an FDA 510(k) cleared B3 GEL System in June 2025, reported first US clinical use in January 2026 and raised a $30M Series A in July 2026. Success to date rests on deep scientific founders and a regulatory milestone rather than traction, since commercial sales only began around the end of 2025. No acquisition, layoffs or shutdown were found.
notes: Series A reported by InnovationMap (article dated 2026-07-28) and by Medical Device Network; the YC page gives July 20, 2026 and the release July 21, 2026. Earlier seed amounts conflict across aggregators (Dealroom $710k and $125k, Village $711K, Caplight $2.55M total, VCBacked $1.1M total) and are unverified, so no seed round is recorded. A 2022 NIH R43 grant for an ECM spray was seen only in a search snippet of a grant database, amount not seen, so it is not recorded as a round. The Seprafilm competitor entry rests on a search snippet of a 2021 review that was not opened in full. Company site does not name founders or explain the name.
